review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. West Coast species and habitat references now replace the generic regulations page; SST evidence is life-stage limited and depth/reef proxies are only partly supported.

profile.size: Min limit None / Bag limit 3-7 per harvester / day
profile.diet: Small fish, crustaceans, squids, and pelagic prey
profile.behavior: Navigates West Coast kelp forests, rocky reefs, and coastal upwelling zones.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for black rockfish.
factors.value_notes: Published early-life studies report young black rockfish occupying a broad nearshore thermal environment (approximately 8-18 °C in summer estuaries and nearshore habitats, with offshore winter/spring waters around 14-15 °C). These are juvenile habitat observations, not adult preferred SST or a catch-response curve; they do not validate the configured 7-15 °C range or 9-13 °C ideal for all life stages.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for black rockfish.
factors.value_notes: WDFW reports black rockfish to 366 m but most commonly shallower than about 73 m; ODFW describes schooling over rocky reefs from bottom to surface and common depths of 0-40 fathoms. This supports the broad 5-80 m outer screening range, but does not establish the 7-75 m ideal as a preferred bottom-depth curve.

factors.reason_template: Seafloor curvature marks sharp reef edges and high-relief pinnacles.
factors.value_notes: WDFW and ODFW describe black rockfish schooling around rocky reefs, pinnacles and kelp. That supports rocky-reef habitat association, but does not directly validate the runtime bottom_curvature metric or a monotonic higher-is-better response.
